cards.explanation: The answer is False. John says, "There were ten royal crowns on its horns and blasphemous names on its heads." So the crowns go on the horns, and the heads carry the names. This beast has a very strange idea of where accessories belong, friends.

The answer is the dragon. John says, "And the dragon gave the beast his power and his throne and great authority." The dragon is the devil and Satan (Revelation 12:9). So the power, the throne and the authority were all handed to the beast.

The answer is healed. John says one head "…appeared to have been mortally wounded. But the mortal wound was healed…" That's the turn in the verse, friends. The wound was deadly, and then it was healed.
The answer is True. John says, "…the mortal wound was healed, and the whole world marveled and followed the beast." First the wound is healed. Then the whole world marvels, and it follows.

The answer is False. John says, "They worshiped the dragon who had given authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast…" So the crowd worships both the dragon and the beast, friends. Never is a strong word, and the text shows it isn't true here.

The answer is that nobody can stand against the beast. That's how the crowd's words come across when they ask, "Who is like the beast, and who can wage war against it?" It's a question with an answer already built in: nobody. And just before this, the verse says the whole world marveled and followed the beast (Revelation 13:3).
The answer is 42. The beast was given "…authority to act for 42 months." Notice the words "was given" again, friends. Whatever it does has a limit placed on it.

The answer is God. John says the beast opened its mouth "…to speak blasphemies against God and to slander His name and His tabernacle…" It's a hard thing to hear, friends. The words are aimed straight at God.

The answer is every tribe and nation on earth, and it's a big reach. John says the beast "…was given authority over every tribe and people and tongue and nation." This is a heavy verse, friends. It names every tribe, people, tongue and nation.

The answer is the Book of Life. John says it's "…the Book of Life belonging to the Lamb who was slain." The names in it were written "…from the foundation of the world…" The Lamb is Jesus (John 1:29).

The answer is that it's a call for the saints to persevere in faith. After the hard word about captivity and the sword, John writes, "Here is a call for the perseverance and faith of the saints." It's a heavy part of the passage, friends. The call is to keep going, with faith.

The answer is a dragon, and that's the twist. This beast "…had two horns like a lamb, but spoke like a dragon." It looks one way and sounds another. Never judge a cookie by how it looks in the box, bakers.

The answer is True. John says the second beast "…caused the earth and those who dwell in it to worship the first beast…" It's also using all the first beast's authority, friends. It works for the first beast.
The answer is deceives. John says, "…it deceived those who dwell on the earth…" The signs it was given to perform are what it uses, friends. The signs were real enough to fool people.

The answer is an image. John says the beast deceived people "…telling them to make an image to the beast that had been wounded by the sword and yet had lived." The people are told to build it, friends. Then it gets breath (Revelation 13:15).

The answer is breath. The second beast "…was permitted to give breath to the image of the first beast, so that the image could speak…" Notice "permitted" again, friends. The text says it was allowed to do this.

The answer is the right hand or the forehead. John says the mark goes "…on their right hand or on their forehead…" Those are the two places named, friends. The second beast requires it of "all people."

The answer is that no one could buy or sell without it. That's the reason the text gives. The mark is required "…so that no one could buy or sell unless he had the mark…" Without it, no buying and no selling, friends. It touches everyday life.

The answer is False. John says no one could buy or sell "…unless he had the mark…" and he names it as the name of the beast or the number of its name. So the mark is tied to the beast's name or the number of its name, friends. The dragon's name isn't in the verse.

The answer is 666. John says, "…for it is the number of a man, and that number is 666." He opens with, "Here is a call for wisdom…" so the number comes with a call to think, friends. That's a good place to end the passage.
